strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem: post-training quantization (PTQ) specifically tailored for Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures in real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR), where fine texture preservation is paramount.

Technically sound and well-motivated framework: H-SVD effectively preserves high-frequency local textures by combining global low-rank SVD with local block-wise rank-1 decomposition under a matched parameter budget.

Principled spatio-temporal mixed-precision strategy: VaSMP provides a calibration-free, rate-distortion guided allocation for layer-wise weight bit-widths, while VaTMP effectively leverages temporal variance dynamics across diffusion timesteps via dynamic programming.

Thorough quantitative and qualitative validation across four standard Real-ISR benchmarks (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250), demonstrating significant perceptual advantages over generic and diffusion PTQ baselines under aggressive W4A6 and W4A4 settings.
weaknesses: Evaluation is limited to a single DiT backbone (DiT4SR). Demonstrating the generalizability of Q-DiT4SR across additional diffusion-based restoration architectures (e.g., DreamClear or latent DiT variants) would strengthen the empirical claims.

Lack of real-world hardware latency benchmarks: While theoretical reductions in FLOPs and model size are reported, mixed-precision weight and dynamically scheduled activation bit-widths across timesteps typically induce kernel-switching and deployment overheads on GPUs/edge accelerators.

Trade-off analysis on distortion metrics: In Table 1(b) under W4A4, SVDQuant achieves better full-reference LPIPS scores than Q-DiT4SR on DrealSR and RealSR, even though Q-DiT4SR dominates on no-reference metrics; a deeper discussion regarding this discrepancy would be beneficial.

strengths: The paper addresses a timely and practically relevant problem: reducing the computational and memory footprint of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) specifically in real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR) via post-training quantization (PTQ).

The proposed H-SVD is well-motivated for super-resolution; decomposing weights into a global low-rank branch and a local block-wise rank-1 branch explicitly addresses the preservation of fine-grained high-frequency details that global low-rank approximations often discard.

The spatio-temporal mixed-precision formulations are theoretically sound and computationally lightweight: VaSMP derives cross-layer weight bit-widths in closed form using rate-distortion theory on Hadamard-transformed weights without requiring calibration data, while VaTMP schedules intra-layer activation bit-widths across timesteps via dynamic programming.

Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments across four real-world SR benchmarks (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250) demonstrate consistent gains over recent PTQ and diffusion quantization baselines (such as QuaRot, SVDQuant, Q-DiT, and FlatQuant), particularly under the aggressive W4A4 setting.
weaknesses: Lack of actual hardware latency and wall-clock benchmarks: The paper reports theoretical parameter reduction and operation counts (FLOPs/Ops), but does not evaluate real-world speedups on target hardware. Mixed precision involving non-power-of-two bit-widths (e.g., 3-bit and 5-bit GEMMs in VaSMP and VaTMP) is notoriously difficult to accelerate on standard GPUs without specialized kernels, and changing activation precision per diffusion timestep introduces runtime scheduling overhead.

Limited architectural diversity: The experimental validation is restricted exclusively to a single backbone (DiT4SR). Evaluating on other DiT-based restoration frameworks (e.g., DreamClear) or analyzing the generalizability of H-SVD to text-to-image DiTs would strengthen the empirical claims.

Missing details on block size selection in SVD-L: In Section 3.2.3, the authors define the search space of feasible block sizes (s_o, s_i) constrained by the parameter budget, but do not specify the exact criterion or objective used to select the best configuration from the feasible set S.
Incomplete text in the abstract: The abstract ends abruptly with 'Our code and models will be available at ' without a link or repository placeholder.

strengths: Well-motivated targeting of DiT-based Real-World Image Super-Resolution (Real-ISR), clearly addressing why standard generic DiT and U-Net post-training quantization methods struggle to retain fine-grained textural details.

Technically sound methodological contributions: Hierarchical SVD (H-SVD) nicely captures both global structure and local high-frequency details under a constrained parameter budget, while the spatio-temporal mixed precision (VaSMP and VaTMP) leverages variance statistics to allocate bit-widths effectively.
Data-free weight bit allocation (VaSMP) and lightweight DP-based activation scheduling (VaTMP) make the approach computationally efficient and easy to calibrate without heavy fine-tuning.

Strong and comprehensive empirical evaluation across four real-world benchmarks (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250) under both W4A6 and aggressive W4A4 regimes, supported by convincing visual comparisons and step-by-step ablations.
weaknesses: Lack of actual on-device hardware latency and memory benchmarking: The reported speedups are based on theoretical operations (Ops/FLOPs) and parameter counts. In practice, per-timestep activation bit switching (VaTMP) and mixed-precision linear layers (VaSMP) can incur kernel switching and hardware scheduling overhead unless specialized GEMM kernels are implemented.

Evaluation is restricted to a single base architecture (DiT4SR). Demonstrating generalization across other DiT-based restoration frameworks (e.g., DreamClear) or text-to-image DiTs would further substantiate the broad applicability of H-SVD and spatio-temporal scheduling.

Missing deployment details regarding SVD-L execution: It is slightly ambiguous whether the block-wise rank-1 matrices WSVD-L are materialized offline into the unquantized branch or computed as separate dynamic block-wise factorized operations during forward inference.

strengths: Timely and practically relevant problem: applying aggressive post-training quantization (W4A6 and W4A4) to Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) specialized for real-world image super-resolution, an area where high-frequency textures are especially prone to degradation.

Technically sound methodology: H-SVD sensibly combines global low-rank approximation with local block-wise rank-1 decomposition to capture both coarse structures and local high-frequency textures; VaSMP and VaTMP offer principled, variance-driven mixed-precision scheduling for cross-layer weights (data-free) and intra-layer activations across timesteps (via dynamic programming).

Comprehensive empirical validation: the method is evaluated on four real-world benchmarks (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250) against a broad set of recent PTQ baselines (SVDQuant, QuaRot, Q-DiT, PTQ4DiT, FlatQuant, etc.), consistently demonstrating strong qualitative and quantitative performance.

Detailed system profiling and thorough ablations: includes actual runtime and peak memory profiling on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with a Triton kernel implementation, alongside clear ablations isolating the impact of H-SVD rank, VaSMP, VaTMP, and calibration set sensitivity.
weaknesses: Ambiguity in real-hardware execution of mixed precision: Section 4.6 notes that arbitrary-precision kernels (e.g., W3/W5) are not natively used and are instead mapped to standard low-bit linear computations. It is not fully clarified how the runtime measurements in Tables 5 and 6 handle the non-power-of-two bitwidths (e.g., 3-bit or 5-bit layers) in hardware without emulated overhead.

Mixed results on full-reference metrics: Under the W4A4 setting (Table 1b), SVDQuant achieves better LPIPS scores on DrealSR (0.3821 vs. 0.4327) and RealSR (0.3268 vs. 0.3665), despite Q-DiT4SR winning on no-reference metrics (MUSIQ, MANIQA, LIQE). A deeper analysis explaining this discrepancy between distortion-oriented perceptual metrics (LPIPS) and no-reference quality metrics would strengthen the paper.

Additional parameter and memory overhead of H-SVD: While the parameter budget of the local branch is constrained, the dual-branch SVD structure introduces extra parameters and memory footprint (3974.64 MiB vs. 3722.83 MiB for SVDQuant in Table 5), which partially offsets the compression gains.

strengths: Addresses an important and challenging problem: deploying Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures for real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR) under aggressive post-training quantization (PTQ) such as W4A6 and W4A4.

The proposed Hierarchical SVD (H-SVD) provides an intuitive and effective decomposition that pairs a global low-rank component with block-wise rank-1 local approximations to retain high-frequency details crucial for image restoration.

The variance-aware mixed-precision formulations are well-grounded: VaSMP provides a closed-form continuous relaxation based on rate-distortion theory requiring zero calibration data for cross-layer weight allocation, while VaTMP effectively uses dynamic programming to capture temporal sensitivity of activations across diffusion steps.

Extensive experimental evaluation across four real-world datasets (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250) against a wide array of recent PTQ baselines (SVDQuant, QuaRot, FlatQuant, Q-DiT, PTQ4DiT, etc.), showing consistent improvements in perceptual and fidelity metrics.

Realistic hardware profiling and system considerations: provides actual peak memory and latency benchmarks on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, a runtime breakdown across operators, and Triton kernel implementation details for the structured block-wise branch.

Thorough ablation and diagnostic experiments, including calibration domain robustness across multiple datasets, generalization to an alternative backbone (DreamClear), and localized ROI artifact analysis.
weaknesses: Practical deployment limitations of non-standard bit-widths: as noted in the limitations discussion, modern Tensor Cores lack native execution support for arbitrary bit-widths like 3-bit or 5-bit activations/weights, meaning practical deployment currently requires mapping to standard precision containers or specialized custom kernels.

Lack of user perceptual studies: given the acknowledged discrepancies between certain no-reference IQA metrics (e.g., MANIQA) and actual visual quality on generative restoration models, a formal subjective user study would have provided stronger validation for the texture preservation claims.

Memory and latency overhead from the dual-branch SVD: although the Triton kernel mitigates much of the cost, maintaining unquantized floating-point global and local branches introduces additional memory footprint and computation relative to pure uniform low-bit baselines.

Evaluation is restricted to a single degradation task setting (x4 super-resolution); evaluating other scaling factors (e.g., x2, x8) or related DiT-based restoration tasks (e.g., deblurring or inpainting) would have further demonstrated the generalizability of the framework.

strengths: Addresses an important and emerging problem: quantizing Diffusion Transformers specifically for Real-World Image Super-Resolution (Real-ISR), where preserving fine-grained high-frequency details is notoriously difficult under low bit-widths.

The proposed Hierarchical SVD (H-SVD) is well-motivated: decomposing residual weights into block-wise rank-1 local approximations under a matched parameter budget effectively recovers localized high-frequency texture information that standard global SVD misses.

The spatio-temporal mixed-precision schemes are theoretically grounded and practical: VaSMP performs cross-layer weight bit allocation offline without requiring calibration data, while VaTMP formulates intra-layer activation precision scheduling across diffusion timesteps as a dynamic programming problem with minimal calibration overhead.

Extensive experimental evaluation across four real-world benchmarks (DrealSR, RealSR, RealLR200, RealLQ250) against a broad set of strong baselines (QuaRot, SVDQuant, Q-DiT, PTQ4DiT, etc.), accompanied by thorough ablation studies, cross-architecture generalization (DreamClear), and calibration robustness analyses.
Includes practical hardware execution profiling with a Triton kernel implementation, measuring real GPU memory footprint reductions and end-to-end inference speedup (reaching ~4.5x on an RTX 4090).
weaknesses: Under the W4A4 regime in Table 1(b), while Q-DiT4SR outperforms baselines across no-reference metrics (MUSIQ, CLIPIQA, LIQE), SVDQuant achieves better full-reference LPIPS on DrealSR (0.3821 vs. 0.4327) and RealSR (0.3268 vs. 0.3665). A more in-depth discussion regarding this trade-off between perceptual fidelity and reference distortion would strengthen the analysis.

Real hardware efficiency of non-standard bit-widths: as noted in the limitations, arbitrary integer bit-widths resulting from VaSMP and VaTMP (such as 3-bit or 5-bit) often lack native tensor core acceleration and are mapped to standard execution; thus, demonstrating how mixed-precision schedules specifically translate into end-to-end latency gains relative to uniform W4A4 remains partially unresolved.

The baseline comparisons could more strictly control for parameter overhead: H-SVD introduces additional local low-rank parameters (totaling ~465M parameters versus ~359M in QuaRot/QueST), so comparing against slightly higher-rank global SVD baselines with equivalent parameter budgets would provide an even fairer assessment.
